item.title: The Exact Central-Index Profile of Groups with Bounded Noncommutativity
item.description: arXiv:2611.00943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a finite group $G$, let $\omega(G)$ be the largest size of a pairwise noncommuting set and put $z(G)=[G:\mathrm Z(G)]$. We determine the maximum possible central index under $\omega(G)\le k$ for every integer $k\ge1$, giving an exact answer to Neumann's central-index question and sharpening Pyber's exponential upper bound. The maximum is $1$ for $k=1,2$, $(k-1)^2$ for $3\le k\le6$, $81$ for $k=7,8$, and $4^{\lfloor(k-1)/2\rfloor}$ for $k\ge9$. In the last range, with $r=\lfloor(k-1)/2\rfloor$, equality holds exactly when $G'\cong C_2$ and $G/\mathrm Z(G)\cong\mathbb F_2^{2r}$. We also obtain the sharp universal bound $z(G)\le(81/64)2^{\omega(G)-1}$. All maximizers are classified up to isoclinism. The results extend to arbitrary groups with finite clique number through finite isoclinic representatives.
item.dc:creator: Guillaume Lecomte

item.title: Generating the liftable outer automorphism groups of regular cyclic covers
item.description: arXiv:2611.01444v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $R_n = \bigvee_{i=1}^{n} S^1$ be a finite connected one-dimensional CW complex with $n \geq 2$, and let $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)$ be the outer automorphism group of the free group $F_n$, where $\pi_1(R_n)\cong F_n$. Let $p_k:\tilde{R}_n\rightarrow R_n$ be the standard $k$-sheeted regular cyclic cover of $R_n$ induced by a $\mathbb{Z}_k$-action on $\tilde{R}_n$ (which is homotopy equivalent to $R_{n_k}$, where $n_k=k(n-1)+1$) generated by a free rotation through $2\pi/k$ of $\tilde{R}_n$. Let $\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)$ be the liftable outer automorphism group associated with a standard $k$-sheeted normal cover $p_k$. For $n\geq3$, we show that $\{\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)\}_{k\geq2}$ forms an infinite family of self-normalizing subgroups of $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)$. For $n\geq2$, these groups are maximal if and only if $k$ is prime. Furthermore, we derive explicit finite generating sets for $\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)$ for $k\geq 2$ and $n\geq 3$. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the infinite chain of roses, and let $q_n:\mathcal{C}\longrightarrow R_n$ be the standard infinite-sheeted cover induced by $\langle \tau\rangle$, where $\tau$ is the unit translation on $\mathcal{C}$. As a final application, we obtain a finite generating set for $\mathrm{Out}_{F_\infty}(F_n)$ when $n\geq 3$.
item.dc:creator: Rohan Suresh Mahure, Priyavrat Pandey, Kashyap Rajeevsarathy

item.title: A faithful representation and profinite completion
item.description: arXiv:2611.01672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We exhibit two finitely generated residually finite groups $G_1$ and $G_2$ with isomorphic profinite completions $\widehat{G_1} \cong \widehat{G_2}$, such that $G_1$ has a faithful representation into $GL(d,\mathbb{C})$ but $G_2$ is not linear. This answers a question of Andrei Jaikin-Zapirain, Alexander Lubotzky, and Martin Bridson negatively. We also present two finitely generated residually finite groups $H_1$ and $H_2$ with isomorphic profinite completions $\widehat{H_1} \cong \widehat{H_2}$ satisfying the following. For every field $k$ with characteristic $p \geq 5$ and transcendence degree $r \geq 2$, there exists $d>0$ such that $H_1$ has a faithful representation into $GL(d,k)$. However, $H_2$ admits no faithful finite-dimensional representation over any field of positive characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Wonyong Jang

item.title: Chain Conditions for Abelian Normal Subgroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.01964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate various chain conditions for abelian normal subgroups of groups, following Robinson (1968). We focus on the maximal condition for abelian normal subgroups, an exceptional case excluded from his results except for some counterexamples. In particular we show that a hypercentral group satisfies the maximal condition for abelian normal subgroups if and only if it is is finitely generated nilpotent.
item.dc:creator: Falih A. M. Aldosray, Ian Stewart

item.title: A proof of the sharpness conjectures for all saturated fusion systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.02043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the D\'iaz$\unicode[Arial]{x2013}$Park conjecture for sharpness of saturated fusion systems. More generally, for every saturated fusion system $\mathcal F$ over a finite $p$-group and every Mackey functor for $\mathcal F$ over the localisation $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ of the integers at $p$, the higher limits of its contravariant part over the centric orbit category vanish in all positive degrees. In particular, the subgroup and normaliser decompositions of every $p$-local finite group $(S,\mathcal F,\mathcal L)$ over the $\mathcal F$-centric subgroups are sharp. This answers in the affirmative a question in the list of important open problems in [M. Aschbacher, R. Kessar and B. Oliver, Fusion Systems in Algebra and Topology, Cambridge Univ. Press (2011)], and proves the sharpness conjecture stated in [M. Aschbacher and B. Oliver, Fusion systems, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (2016)] and Conjecture 1.2 of [E. Yal\c{c}$\unicode[Arial]{x131}$n, Higher limits over the fusion orbit category, Adv. Math. (2022)]. The proof is algebraic and does not rely on the classification of finite simple groups.
item.dc:creator: Baoyu Zhang, Shengmin Zhang

item.title: $M$-subgroups and normal-subgroup lattices of finite groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.02078v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a group. A normal subgroup $E$ is an $M$-subgroup if $E\cap N_1\cap N_2\neq1$ whenever $N_1\cap N_2$, $E\cap N_1$, and $E\cap N_2$ are non-trivial for normal subgroups $N_1,N_2$. We characterise these subgroups as the essential or relatively uniform normal subgroups. For finite $G$, an $M$-subgroup is either trivial, contains exactly one minimal normal subgroup, or contains the socle. Consequently, every normal subgroup is an $M$-subgroup precisely when the socle has $G$-chief length at most two. We obtain an explicit $M$-closure operation and describe the minimal normal subgroups of finite direct products. For crown-based powers, we use the known comparability of normal subgroups with the socle to describe the normal lattice in terms of Boolean or subspace lattices and the quotient above the socle. We then determine when the $M$-lattice retains the normal lattice, classify normal quotients and their automorphism orbits, and characterise quotient maps compatible with $M$-closure. Finally, we compute the maximal length of chains of $M$-subgroups in terms of the chief length and socle length of $G$.
item.dc:creator: Annesh Nag, Pronay Biswas, Amartya Goswami

item.title: Finite Groups with Few Almost Maximal Subgroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.02532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group. L. Morgana, C. E. Praeger, A.E. Zalesski \cite {MOR} introduced the notion of almost maximal subgroup of $G$. A subgroup $H$ of $G$ is said to be almost maximal in $G$ if $N_G(H)$ is maximal in $G$. In this paper, let $AM(G)$ denote the number of conjugacy classes of all almost maximal subgroups of $G$. First, we prove that $G$ is Dedekindian if and only if $AM(G)=0$. Second, we show that the finite groups with $AM(G)\leq 1$ are supersolvable. Furthermore, we characterize the structure of finite groups with $AM(G)=1$. Final, we investigate a lower bound of $AM(G)$ for certain non-solvable groups.
item.dc:creator: Wei Meng, Boru Zhang, Jiakuan Lu

item.title: On a finite group in which every maximal subgroup of order divisible by $p$ containing the normalizer of some Sylow subgroup is nilpotent
item.description: arXiv:2611.02596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group and $p$ any fixed prime divisor of $|G|$. We prove that if every maximal subgroup of $G$ of order divisible by $p$ containing the normalizer of some Sylow subgroup is nilpotent then $G$ is a solvable group having a Sylow tower and $G$ is $q$-nilpotent or $q$-closed for each prime divisor $q$ of $|G|$.
item.dc:creator: Jiangtao Shi, Fanghua Li

item.title: A note on an extension of Shidov's theorem and Shlyk's theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.02608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a non-solvable group and $p$ any fixed prime divisor of $|G|$. We prove that the intersection of all non-nilpotent maximal subgroups of $G$ of order divisible by $p$ containing the normalizer of some Sylow subgroup is $p$-closed, which provides a further generalization of Shidov's theorem and Shlyk's theorem.
item.dc:creator: Jiangtao Shi, Fanghua Li

item.title: Buildings governed by twisted Bruhat orders
item.description: arXiv:2611.02925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces the notion of a twisted building associated to a Coxeter system and an initial section of a reflection order. These are pairs of buildings and a map between them which depends on a twisted Bruhat order. It is proved that projection maps exist between components and that the common apartment property holds for a suitable notion of an apartment, generalising what is known for twin buildings. Several well-known examples are given, including a family of twisted buildings associated to an affine building and its fa\c{c}ades.
item.dc:creator: Harvey Sykes

item.title: Digital Finite Group Theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.03074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This book develops a digital formulation of finite group theory, in which every finite group of order $N$ is represented as the alphabet $\{0,1,\dots,N-1\}$ endowed with the transported group product. Multiplication, inversion and related structure are written explicitly as integer operations on labels. The foundations treat digit functions, codes of permutations and $r$-ary operators, finite magmas, and constructions of laws from diagrams. Classical parts of finite group theory, including conjugacy classes, stabiliser chains and characters, are recast as identities between digits of codes. The book gives explicit digital laws for all groups of order at most 32, the finite quotients of the 17 plane and 230 space crystallographic groups, the symmetric and alternating groups, the finite simple groups of Lie type, and all 26 sporadic groups. For most sporadic groups the laws are obtained by chain constructions; for the Baby Monster and the Monster they are computed structurally from the 196884-dimensional representation and evaluated with the mmgroup package. The accompanying software archive reproduces the laws, tables and worked examples as verifiable integer data.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Garc\'{\i}a-Morales

item.title: Constructing free subgroups of matrix groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.03175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Tits alternative asserts that a finitely generated linear group is either solvable-by-finite or contains a non-abelian free subgroup. Given a non-solvable-by-finite subgroup G of GL(d, F), where F is the field of complex numbers or a non-archimedean local field, we present methods to construct explicitly a non-abelian 2-generator free subgroup of G in specific cases. Our implementations in the computeralgebra system Oscar are publicly available.
item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Breuillard, Bettina Eick, Tommy Hofmann, Derek Holt, Eamonn O'Brien

item.title: A complete description of the algebraic structure of pseudocompact abelian groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.03270v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We solve a major open problem from [D. Dikranjan, D. Shakhmatov, Algebraic structure of pseudocompact groups, Memoirs AMS 633 (1998)] by describing abelian groups which admit a pseudocompact Hausdorff group topology. First, we prove that an abelian group G can be equipped with a pseudocompact Hausdorff group topology iff it can be decomposed into a direct sum G=B\oplus H of a bounded torsion group B and agroup H satisfying |nH|=|H| for all positive integers $n$, such that both B and H admit a pseudocompact Hausdorff group topology. Second, for an unbounded abelian group G, we denote by m the minimal positive integer n such that |nG|=|kG| for all integers k\ge n. Then G admits a pseudocompact group topology iff both G[m]={g\in G: mg=0} and mG\cong G/G[m] admit a pseudocompact Hausdorff group topology.
item.dc:creator: Dikran Dikranjan, Alejandro Dorantes-Aldama, Dmitri Shakhmatov

item.title: Finite groups with all involutions fused
item.description: arXiv:2611.03366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize finite groups whose involutions form a single fusion class. In the solvable case, we show that the $2$-length is $1$, extending Thompson's theorem which states that a solvable group with all involutions conjugate has $2$-length $1$. For a nonsolvable group $G$, we prove that if its involutions are fused then they are conjugate; moreover, $G/\mathbf{O}_{2'}(G)$ is almost quasisimple. As an application, we obtain a restriction on $m$ for which an $m$-pyramidal Kirkman triple system can be realized under a nonsolvable group.
item.dc:creator: Zheng Guo, Yan Zhou Zhu

item.title: Singular Loci of SL2(C)-Representation Varieties of Non-Hopfian Baumslag--Solitar Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.03402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the singular loci of the reduced $\SL_2(\CC)$-representation varieties $R_{m,n}$ of non-Hopfian Baumslag--Solitar groups $B(m,n)=\langle a,b\mid b^{-1}a^m b=a^n\rangle$. We determine their dimensions and profile functions, which list the numbers of irreducible components in descending order of dimension. The components have dimensions three or five. Their reduced singular loci have the explicit description \[ \Sing R_{m,n} =\left\{(\varepsilon I,Y): \varepsilon^m=\varepsilon^n,\quad (\tr Y)^2=\frac{(m+n)^2}{mn}\right\}, \] where $\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}$ and $Y\in\SL_2(\CC)$. Each is a disjoint union of $\mu$ copies of the smooth affine quadric $Q=\{(x,y,z)\in\CC^3:x^2+yz=1\}$, where $\mu=2$ for $m-n$ odd and $\mu=4$ for $m-n$ even. Thus its complex algebraic isomorphism type depends only on this parity. Each quadric is homotopy equivalent to $S^2$, so the singular locus has integral homology $\ZZ^\mu$ in degrees zero and two and zero in all other degrees. An algebraic stratification gives its compactly supported E-polynomial $\mu(q^2+q)$, with $q=uv$. At every singular point, $R_{m,n}$ is locally analytically the product of a smooth surface and a nodal curve.
item.dc:creator: S. Liriano

item.title: Vanishing-set inclusion and character degrees in finite $p$-groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.03541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite $p$-group and let $\chi,\psi\in\operatorname{Irr}(G)$. We prove that $$\operatorname{Van}(\chi)\subseteq\operatorname{Van}(\psi) \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \chi(1)\mid\psi(1),$$ where $\operatorname{Van}(\theta)=\{g\in G:\theta(g)=0\}$. Consequently, two irreducible characters of a finite $p$-group with the same vanishing set have the same degree. This answers a question attributed to J. Sangroniz and recorded by Hung, Moret\'o, and Morotti, extending the previously known case in which one character has degree $p$. The same divisibility conclusion holds for irreducible characters of finite nilpotent groups.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Lin Zhang

item.title: Diagram of Geodesic Intervals in $C'(1/8)$-Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.00095v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a group characterized by a small cancellation $C'(1/8)$-presentation. We study the structure of its Cayley graph, specifically geodesic intervals and digons. We prove that all geodesic segments $[x,y]$ of length $n$ can be covered by finitely many simple geodesic digons with pairwise $C'(1/8)$-short lower intersections whose lower sides lie on a common geodesic segment $[x,y]$. This is a generalization of a proposition of Kharlampovich-Sklinos (arXiv:2106.05461) for random groups. We then bound this resulting diagram of digons, showing that the total perimeter of its cells and its edge count is bounded by $n$, and the cycle rank is equal to the number of distinct cell contours. Thus, although there may be many different geodesics, the size of their union is bounded linearly in the distance between their endpoints. The constant is independent of the number and lengths of the defining relators. In particular, the estimate applies to infinite presentations with unbounded relator lengths. From this we get a consequence for growth, allowing us to compare the number of geodesic words with the number of group elements of the same length.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Hoffmann

item.title: Some Constructions in the Category of Topological Partial Actions
item.description: arXiv:2611.00363v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present some theoretical aspects of the categories of global and partial group actions of topological groups on topological spaces, denoted by G-ActTop and G-pActTop, respectively. We construct topological partial actions on products and disjoint unions of topological spaces, and G-pinvariant subspaces. Furthermore, we provide an adequate definition of congruence (G-pcongruence), which enables the construction of quotient objects in the category of topological partial actions. In addition, we associate a special G-pcongruence to each pair of strong G-pmorphisms. Then, we study products, co-products, equalizers, co-equalizers, pullbacks, and pushouts in the category G-pActTop. We find that the category of topological partial actions is finitely complete and contains a co-complete subcategory. Finally, we show that the relationship between a topological partial action and its enveloping action is functorial. As a consequence, we obtain that the categorical product in G-ActTop coincides with the categorical product in G-pActTop. Moreover, the envelope of a co-product in G-pActTop is given by the co-product of the respective envelopes.
item.dc:creator: Jes\'us \'Avila, Fabi\'an Molina

item.title: Spectral Fields and Unitary Descent: Local splitting, simultaneous norms, and transcendental obstructions
item.description: arXiv:2611.00456v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spectral fields can recover matrix coefficients without standardizing the invariant Hermitian form. Over an algebraic subfield of $\mathbb{C}$ stable under nontrivial complex conjugation, we prove that every Zariski-dense subgroup in a normalized Hermitian model of dimension $m\ge4$ and signature $(m-1,1)$ at the fixed embedding contains a loxodromic element whose spectrum makes all diagonal coefficients norms. The element can be chosen so that every positive power is regular and generates the same splitting field. For an arbitrary initial Hermitian model over such a field, two spectra suffice for standard unitary descent over an extension of relative degree at most $(m!)^2$. Over every quadratic extension $F/k$ of nonarchimedean local fields of characteristic zero, a four-dimensional quasi-split unitary group of Witt index two contains a discrete, Zariski-dense free subgroup whose spectra all split over $F$. Over intrinsic fields of positive transcendence degree, we construct a single convex cocompact, Zariski-dense free subgroup of $\mathrm{SU}(3,1)$ for which, for every initial regular element and every normalized extraction, the Hermitian obstruction persists after adjoining any finite family of spectra and over the total spectral field.
item.dc:creator: Angel Cano, Nikolay Gusevskii, Marlon M. L\'opez-Flores

item.title: On subgroup perfect codes and regular sets in generalized Cayley graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.00893v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A subset $C$ of the vertex set of a graph $\Gamma$ is said to be an $(a,b)$-regular set if $C$ induces an $a$-regular subgraph and every vertex outside $C$ is adjacent to exactly $b$ vertices in $C$. A $(0,1)$-regular set is called a perfect code. Let $G$ be a finite group and let $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ be such that $\alpha^2=\mathrm{id}$. Let $\omega_\alpha(G)=\{\alpha(g^{-1})g:g\in G\}$. For a subset $S\subseteq G$ satisfying $\alpha(S)=S^{-1}$ and $S\cap\omega_\alpha(G)=\emptyset$, the generalized Cayley graph of $(G,\alpha)$ with respect to $S$ is the graph with vertex set $G$ in which two distinct elements $g,h\in G$ are adjacent if and only if $\alpha(g^{-1})h\in S$. In this paper, we prove two main results. First, let $H$ be an $\alpha$-invariant subgroup of a finite group $G$, and let $P$ be an $\alpha$-invariant Sylow 2-subgroup of $H$. We show that $H$ is a perfect code of $(G,\alpha)$ if and only if $P[H,\alpha]$ is a perfect code of $(G,\alpha)$, where $[H,\alpha]=\langle h^{-1}\alpha(h):h\in H\rangle$. Second, we consider finite groups $G$ possessing a cyclic subgroup $A$ of index 2 that is invariant under an involutory automorphism $\alpha$. We show that $\omega_\alpha(G)$ is a subgroup of $A$. Using this result, we give a complete characterization of all pairs $(a,b)$ for which an $\alpha$-invariant subgroup $H$ of $G$ is an $(a,b)$-regular set of $(G,\alpha)$. In particular, our characterization applies to all finite groups possessing a characteristic cyclic subgroup of index 2, for every involutory automorphism $\alpha$.
item.dc:creator: Yasamin Khaefi, Fateme Sadat Seiedali

item.title: Secant dimensions and bilinear decomposition widths for finite Heisenberg groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.01104v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G=UT_3(\F_q)$ be the finite Heisenberg group. We study the image closures and secant varieties of a family of equivariant bilinear maps between representations induced from central characters. Evaluation at a basepoint identifies the ambient space with $M_{q^2}(\C)$. A single channel is represented by $A^T\operatorname{diag}(d)B$, with $A$ and $B$ in prescribed twisted-convolution algebras. We prove that its affine image closure has dimension $3q^2-2$ for every central-character pair and that its affine second-secant closure has the expected dimension for every prime power $q$. For $q\ge3$, the proof constructs two differential images with zero intersection. We also prove a subgroup-lifting theorem for channel parameterizations on finite abelian groups with bicharacter coefficients: a parameter point with differential rank $r(3|H|-2)$ on a subgroup $H$ extends by zero to a parameter point with differential rank $r(3|K|-2)$ on the ambient group $K$, provided that every parameter vector is nonzero. Exact Jacobian certificates determine all secant dimensions for $q=2,3,4,5$, with generic widths $2,4,6,9$. The lifting theorem yields specified higher-secant dimensions on infinite families of extension fields. Attainment of the dimension lower bound for arbitrary $q$ remains a conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Nguyen Bich Van, Nguyen Trung Kien

item.title: The most singular loci of twisted character varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.01528v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For any simply connected almost simple group $G$ and any compact Riemann surface of genus $g>1$, we study the singular locus of the character variety which parametrises fundamental group representations with a twist by a central element $z$ of $G$. While for $z=1$ the most singular representations have values in a maximal torus (and are invariant for the Weyl group action) and for generic $z$ every $z$-twisted representation is irreducible, for a general $z$ we find that the most singular representations have values in a particular Levi subgroup $L_z$ up to conjugation. From the explicit Lie-theoretic description of $L_z$, we determine the structure of the maximal stabiliser groups, and prove that the most singular loci is a disjoint union of generic type $A$ character varieties.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Shu

item.title: The inductive Navarro-Alperin weight condition for the Suzuki and Ree groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.01608v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we give verifications of the inductive Navarro-Alperin weight condition in [8] for the Suzuki and Ree groups at all primes.
item.dc:creator: Qianhu Zhou

item.title: Quasimorphisms and bounded cohomology of transformation groups of nonorientable surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.02847v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $N_g$ be a closed connected nonorientable surface of genus $g\ge1$, let $\omega$ be a smooth positive density, and let $\mu$ be a good measure. In this paper we generalize the Gambaudo--Ghys construction using homogeneous quasimorphisms on the central quotients of the braid groups of $N_g$. We prove injectivity of this map for density-preserving diffeomorphisms. For $g\ge2$ and quasimorphisms vanishing on the disc braid group, we obtain an injective map to $C^0$-continuous homogeneous quasimorphisms on $Homeo_0(N_g,\mu)$. We also obtain undistortion criteria in $Homeo_0(N_g)$ and $Diff_0(N_g)$. For $g=1,2$ and every $d\ge2$, we prove $$ \dim\overline H_b^d(Homeo_0(N_g,\mu))=\infty,\qquad \dim\overline{EH}_b^d(Diff_0(N_g,\omega))=\infty. $$ Moreover, $\overline{EH}_b^d(Homeo_0(N_2,\mu))$ is infinite dimensional in every positive even degree $d$. Here $\overline{H}_b^d$ and $\overline{EH}_b^d$ denote reduced bounded cohomology and reduced exact bounded cohomology, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Michael Brandenbursky

item.title: Full-Rank Constructions of Explicit Lossless Expanders and Good Small-Set qLTCs
item.description: arXiv:2611.02963v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct explicit two-sided lossless expanders whose binary adjacency matrices have full rank, and use them to obtain explicit asymptotically good quantum LDPC codes whose specified X- and Z-check matrices have full row rank and satisfy small-set soundness, or confinement, on a linear range. Our lossless expanders are a variant of those of Hsieh, Lubotzky, Mohanty, Reiner, and Zhang, with a free action of a finite 2-group. Under such an action, injectivity and surjectivity of the adjacency matrix are detected on a fixed-size matrix indexed by vertex orbits. Adding a sparse factor to the gadget at the middle vertices of a single type then enforces full rank, with a controlled loss in expansion. To obtain the 2-group action, we observe that reducing the generators of the Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak Ramanujan graphs modulo powers of 2, instead of modulo an odd prime, gives Ramanujan Cayley graphs on finite 2-groups. This construction may be of independent interest. Plugging two such expanders into the balanced product of Lin and Hsieh gives the quantum codes, since full rank of the input graphs is inherited by the check matrices. Our construction supplies the code family sought by Hong, Guo, and Lucas. Applying their analysis, within their framework and under their dynamical assumptions, gives quantum memories whose free-energy density is analytic at every positive temperature and whose guaranteed lifetime is $exp(\Omega(N))$ at sufficiently low fixed positive temperature, where N is the blocklength. This improves the previously guaranteed stretched-exponential timescale.
item.dc:creator: Yali Aharon-Holzman, Michael Ilan, Assaf Reiner, Amnon Ta-Shma

item.title: A resolution of the Steinberg module of a parabolic subgroup of GL_n
item.description: arXiv:2611.03303v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let F be a field, G = GL_n(F), and let St be the Steinberg module of G. For a parabolic subgroup P of G, let St_P be its Steinberg module. There is a natural map rho_P: St -> St_P corresponding to intersection of a modular symbol with the Borel--Serre boundary. We construct a ZP-resolution Sh_P of St_P, the P-sharbly resolution. We also construct a P-equivariant chain map from the sharbly resolution of St to the P-sharbly resolution of St_P which enables us to compute the map induced on Steinberg homologies by rho_P. In the case when F is a number field and Gamma subset G is a torsion-free arithmetic subgroup, rho_P induces the restriction map H^(Gamma, E) -> H^(Gamma cap P, E) via Borel--Serre duality, for any coefficient module E which is flat over the base ring. If E is a vector space over Z/pZ this provides a computation of the restriction map on cohomology from Gamma to Gamma cap P in terms of sharblies, which enables the study of this restriction map in characteristic p, where Eisenstein series cannot be used.
item.dc:creator: Avner Ash, Paul E. Gunnells

item.title: Centralizers of maps as automorphism groups of Yang--Baxter solutions
item.description: arXiv:2611.03380v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a partition $X = Y \sqcup Z$ of a set $X$ and an arbitrary map $g \colon Y \to {\rm Hom}_{\rm Set} (Z, \, Z)$, we construct a solution $R_g \colon X \times X \to X \times X$ of the braid equation. We characterize intrinsically the solutions which are isomorphic to some $R_g$ and we give a necessary and sufficient condition for two solutions $R_g$ and $R_{g'}$ to be isomorphic. Consequently, the number of isomorphism classes of the solutions $R_g$ on a set with $n$ elements is $1 + \sum_{k = 1}^{n-1} \widetilde{o} (n - k, \, k)$, where $\widetilde{o} (m, \, k)$ is the number of orbits of the symmetric group $S_m$, acting by conjugation, on the set of multisets with $k$ elements of maps $\{1, \ldots, m\} \to \{1, \ldots, m\}$. This construction is then used to obtain a solution of the braid equation whose automorphism group is exactly the centralizer ${\rm Aut} (f_1, \ldots, f_k)$ of a given family $f_1, \ldots, f_k \colon X \to X$ of maps, $k \geq 1$. For $k = 2$, combined with a result of Agore, Chirvasitu and the author, this gives another proof of the fact that any group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a solution of the braid equation (equivalently, of the set-theoretic Yang--Baxter equation).
item.dc:creator: Gigel Militaru

item.title: $C^1$-rigidity of $\mathbb{H}^{p,q}$-convex cocompact representations of Gromov hyperbolic groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.03539v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $p>3$ and let $\Gamma$ be a non-elementary Gromov hyperbolic group with $\partial_\infty\Gamma\cong\mathbb S^{p-1}$. We prove that every $\mathbb{H}^{p,2}$-convex cocompact representation $$ \rho:\Gamma\longrightarrow \mathrm{PO}_{p,3} $$ whose proximal limit set $\Lambda_\rho\subset\partial_\infty\mathbb{H}^{p,2}$ is a $C^1$ submanifold preserves a totally geodesic copy of $\mathbb{H}^p\subset\mathbb{H}^{p,2}$. Consequently, $\Gamma/\ker \rho$ is virtually a cocompact lattice in $\mathrm{Isom}(\mathbb{H}^p)$. For odd $p$, we prove the same conclusion for every signature $(p,q)$ with $p>q\ge2$, under the same hypothesis $\partial_\infty\Gamma\cong\mathbb S^{p-1}$. Our methods combine dynamics, differential topology, and representation theory. The key new ingredient is to study the radicals of the semidefinite forms induced on the tangent spaces of the limit set. They form a continuous vector bundle of constant rank. The tangent action at attracting fixed points gives a bound, in terms of the radical rank, on the number of eigenvalues of an orthogonal lift whose modulus exceeds one. We then use the topology of the sphere and the representation theory of real algebraic groups to exclude the remaining possibilities. In arbitrary signature with $p>q$, these arguments already imply that a representation with a $C^1$ limit set cannot be Zariski dense.
item.dc:creator: Nikolay Bogachev

item.title: Associated primes in group cohomology and a strange result
item.description: arXiv:2611.03569v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In 2010. Okuyama proved the following. Let $G$ be a finite group and $k$ an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$ dividing the order of $G$. (1) Let $\frak p$ be an associated prime of $H^*(G,k)$ of $\dim=s$. Then there exists an elementary abelian $p$-subgroup $E\subseteq G$ of rank $s$ with $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p_E$ and depth$\,H^*(C_GE,k)=s$. (2) Let $E$ be an elementary abelian $p$-subgroup of $G$ of rank $s$ and suppose depth$\,H^*(C_GE,k)=s$. Then $\mathfrak p_E$ is an associated prime of $H^*(G,k)$. It is shown this result is true for all fields of characteristic $p$. We also show the following result: If $E$ is an elementary abelian $p$-subgroup of $G$ and depth $H^*(G,k)=\text{rank} E$, then up to conjugation $E$ contains the maximal elementary abelian subgroup contained in the center of a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$.
item.dc:creator: James A. Schafer

item.title: Discrete two-generator subgroups of ${\rm PSL_2}$ over non-archimedean local fields
item.description: arXiv:2208.12404v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K$ be a non-archimedean local field with residue field of characteristic $p$. We give necessary and sufficient conditions for a two-generator subgroup $G$ of ${\rm PSL_2}(K)$ to be discrete, where either $K=\mathbb{Q}_p$ or $G$ contains no elements of order $p$. We give a practical algorithm to decide whether such a subgroup $G$ is discrete. We also give practical algorithms to decide whether a two-generator subgroup of either ${\rm SL_2}(\mathbb{R})$ or ${\rm SL_2}(K)$ (where $K$ is a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$) is dense. A crucial ingredient for this work is a structure theorem for two-generator groups acting by isometries on a $\Lambda$-tree.
item.dc:creator: Matthew J. Conder, Jeroen Schillewaert

item.title: On the number of conjugacy classes of subgroups of a finite group
item.description: arXiv:2508.14267v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $k'(G)$ and $L(G)$ be the number of conjugacy classes of subgroups and the subgroup lattice of a finite group $G$, respectively. Our objective is to study some aspects related to the ratios $d'(G)=\frac{k'(G)}{|L(G)|}$ and $d^*(G)=\min\{ d'(S) \mid S\text{ is a section of }G\}$ which measure how close $G$ is to being a Dedekind group. We prove that the set containing the values $d'(G)$, as $G$ ranges over the class of nilpotent groups, is dense in $[0, 1]$. A nilpotency criterion is obtained by proving that if $d^*(G)>\frac{2}{3}$, then $G$ is nilpotent and information on its structure is given. We also show that if $d^*(G)>\frac{4}{5}$, then $G$ is an Iwasawa group. Finally, we deduce a result which ensures that a $p$-group of order $p^n$ ($n\geq 3$) is a Dedekind group. This last result can be extended to the class of nilpotent groups and it also highlights the second maximum value of $d^*$ on the class of $p$-groups of order $p^n$.
item.dc:creator: Mihai-Silviu Lazorec, Marius T\u{a}rn\u{a}uceanu

item.title: Probabilistic Hanna Neumann Conjectures
item.description: arXiv:2601.00053v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a theory of polymatroids on Stallings core graphs, and prove a gap theorem. As special cases of it, we prove the gap conjecture of Ernst-West, Puder, Seidel and the author on the stable $K$-primitivity rank (using a forthcoming result of Ernst-West and Puder); prove Reiter's conjecture on word-random subgroups of finite groups; improve Bowen's bounds on the $f$-invariant for p.m.p. actions of free groups in which a generating partition has a non-cyclic stabilizer, deducing coalescence; and extend the proof of Wise's $w$-cycle conjecture by Louder and Wilton to not-necessarily-cyclic subgroups, which gives a new proof of this special case of the Friedman-Mineyev theorem (i.e. the Hanna Neumann conjecture). Louder and Wilton further improved the bound in Wise's conjecture via their "dependence theorem"; in an appendix joint with Noam Ta Shma, we extend this improvement too to not-necessarily-cyclic subgroups, again as a special case of the main gap theorem. We also compute the exact decay rate of the expected number of invariant subsets, respectively subspaces, for word-random subgroups of $S_n$, respectively $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$.
item.dc:creator: Yotam Shomroni, Noam Ta Shma

item.title: Minimum $\mathcal{F}$-covers: the supersolvable and metabelian cases
item.description: arXiv:2602.06220v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a set $\mathcal{F}$ of finite groups, it is said that a group $G$ is an $\mathcal{F}$-cover if every group in $\mathcal{F}$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of $G$. Moreover, $G$ is a minimum $\mathcal{F}$-cover if there is no $\mathcal{F}$-cover whose order is less than $|G|$. In [Cameron P. J., et al., Minimal cover groups, J. Algebra 660 (2024)], the authors pose the following question: For which classes $\mathcal{X}$ of groups, closed under taking subgroups and direct products, is it true that, if $\mathcal{F}$ is a set of $\mathcal{X}$-groups, then there is a minimum $\mathcal{F}$-cover which is an $\mathcal{X}$-group? In this paper, we give a negative answer in two cases: $\mathcal{X}\in \{``supersolvable", ``metabelian"\}.$
item.dc:creator: Mihai-Silviu Lazorec

item.title: On some problems regarding $LCM$-groups
item.description: arXiv:2602.06228v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group and denote by $o(g)$ the order of an element $g\in G$. We say that $G$ is an $LCM$-group if $o(x^ny)$ is a divisor of the least common multiple of $o(x^n)$ and $o(y)$ for all $x, y\in G$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$. This paper extends some existing results on $LCM$-groups, such as the structure of a minimal non-$LCM$-group, and establishes criteria for $G$ to be an $LCM$-group or a nilpotent group. We also prove that, in general, a minimum cover of a finite set of $LCM$-groups is not an $LCM$-group, and we answer two questions posed by M. Amiri.
item.dc:creator: Mihai-Silviu Lazorec

item.title: On the triple product property for subgroups of finite groups of nilpotency class $2$
item.description: arXiv:2602.15796v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Some non-trivial upper bounds are proved relating to the triple product property (TPP) for subgroups of finite nilpotent groups of class $2$ using elementary group theory. The TPP is the property defined for three non-empty subsets $S, T, U$ of a group $G$ that the group equation $s's^{-1}t't^{-1}u'u^{-1} = 1$, over pairs of elements $s', s \in S$, $t', t \in T$, $u', u \in U$, is satisfied if and only if $s' = s$, $t' = t$, $u' = u$. When $G$ is finite, and the parameter $\rho_0(G)$, called \emph{subgroup TPP ratio}, is defined as $\rho_0(G) := \max\frac{|S||T||U|}{|G|}$, where the maximum is over the collection of all triples of subgroups $S, T, U$ of $G$ satisfying the TPP, this paper proves that \textup{(1)} $\rho_0(G) < \sqrt{G:Z(G)}$} for (all) groups of nilpotency class $2$, \textup{(2)} $\rho_0(G) \leq p$ for $p$-groups with a cyclic commutator subgroup of order $p$, \textup{(3)} $\rho_0(G) = 1$ for $p$-groups of nilpotency class $2$ with a "large" centre such that either $G/Z(G)$ is isomorphic to $C_p \times C_p$ or $C_{p^2} \times C_p$, \textup{(4)} and $\rho_0(G) = 1$ for $p$-groups of nilpotency class $2$ with "small" (irreducible, complex) character degrees of $1$ or $p$ where $G/Z(G)$ is not isomorphic to $C_p \times C_p \times C_p$.
item.dc:creator: Sandeep R. Murthy

item.title: From cut sets to cube complexes
item.description: arXiv:2603.20424v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we obtain an action on a cube complex from an action on a path-connected topological space with a system of divisions. In the settings of hyperbolic groups or relatively hyperbolic groups with no peripheral splittings, our result provides an alternate route to Sageev's construction of a cube complex action from a collection of (relatively) quasiconvex subgroups of a (relatively) hyperbolic group.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Haulmark, Jason Fox Manning

item.title: A family of groups extending McLain's
item.description: arXiv:2604.02087v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a strict partial order $\Delta$ on a set $\Lambda$ and an arbitrary ring $R$ with $1\neq 0$, the corresponding McLain group $M(\Delta)$ has been studied in depth. We construct a larger family of McLain groups $G(\Delta)$, where $\Delta$ need be neither asymmetric nor transitive, while satisfying two weaker axioms. Structural properties common to all members~$G(\Delta)$ of this new family are investigated, including a group presentation, a description of the factors of its descending central series, a canonical form for its elements relative to any total order on~$\Delta$, and a recursive determination of its upper central series. In addition, we prove the natural isomorphism $G(\Delta)/G(\Gamma)\cong G(\Delta\setminus\Gamma)$, where $\Gamma$ is a normal subset of $\Delta$, and $G(\Gamma)$ and $G(\Delta\setminus\Gamma)$ are extended McLain groups on their own right. This result has no parallel in the classical context.
item.dc:creator: Leandro Cagliero, Fernando Szechtman

item.title: Cost of one-relator groups
item.description: arXiv:2606.23506v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For any infinite one-relator group $\Gamma=\langle S \mid w^m\rangle$, we prove that $\mathrm{cost}(\Gamma)=|S|-\frac{1}{m}$. For such groups, this gives $\beta^{(2)}_1(\Gamma)=\mathrm{cost}(\Gamma) - 1$, answering a special case of Gaboriau's question on the relationship between cost and first $\ell^2$-Betti number.
item.dc:creator: Antoine Poulin, Konrad Wr\'obel

item.title: Infinite Girth, Finite Quotients, and Nielsen Connectivity in Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.10925v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop new methods for studying infinite girth in finitely generated residually finite groups, particularly those containing no non-abelian free subgroups and satisfying no non-trivial group law. Our main contribution is a probabilistic Nielsen-component lifting principle, based on product replacement graphs, which provides a criterion for transferring suitable generation and word-avoidance properties of finite quotients to the ambient group. As an application, we prove that every finitely generated group admitting infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic non-abelian finite simple quotients has infinite girth, with extensions to quasisimple and, under additional hypotheses, almost-simple quotients. We further establish infinite girth for the B. H. Neumann group and the Bou-Rabee-Seward group, obtaining new results on the occurrence of non-abelian finite simple quotients and sections. By a different construction, we also prove that Alt_fin(Z) semidirect Z has infinite girth. Finally, we establish a marked finite-quotient characterization of infinite girth for finitely generated residually finite groups and prove that, for linear groups over fields of characteristic zero, large marked girth can be realized in congruence quotients. We conclude with several open questions and remarks arising from our results.
item.dc:creator: Pratyush Mishra

item.title: Regular automorphisms of periodic $p'$-groups need not be splitting
item.description: arXiv:2610.15360v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a fixed prime $p$, a group is called a $p'$-group if the orders of all its elements are coprime to $p$. It is well known that in a finite $p'$-group an automorphism of order $p$ is regular if and only if it is a splitting automorphism of period $p$. In the Kourovka Notebook, V.\,D.~Mazurov asked whether these two notions coincide for periodic $p'$-groups. We answer this question in the negative by constructing a periodic group of prime period $q$ that admits a regular automorphism of order $p \neq q$ which is not splitting.
item.dc:creator: V. S. Atabekyan

item.title: When do lazy and invertible cellular automata generate all cellular automata?
item.description: arXiv:2610.18480v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a group and let $A$ be a set with at least two elements. A lazy cellular automaton over $A^G$ acts as the identity except at the cells where a fixed pattern occurs, where it replaces the central symbol by a fixed different symbol. Let $M(G;A)$ be the submonoid of $\mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ generated by the lazy and the invertible cellular automata. We study when $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. Since no lazy cellular automaton is surjective, every surjective element of $M(G;A)$ is invertible; hence $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ whenever $A$ is infinite or $G$ has an element of infinite order. More unexpectedly, if $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has a quotient isomorphic to the Klein four-group $C_2 \times C_2$, then $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. For locally finite groups, these are the only obstructions: we prove that $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ if and only if $3 \leq |A| < \infty$, or $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has no quotient isomorphic to $C_2 \times C_2$.
item.dc:creator: Edgar Alcal\'a-Arroyo, Alonso Castillo-Ramirez

item.title: On the residual polynilpotence of tree products of groups with locally cyclic edge subgroups
item.description: arXiv:2610.23126v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{N}$ be a non-empty class of nilpotent groups closed under taking subgroups, quotient groups, finite direct products, and unrestricted direct powers of the form $\prod_{x \in X}Y_{x}$, where $X \in \mathcal{N}$ and $Y_{x}$ ($x \in X$) are isomorphic copies of a group $Y \in \mathcal{N}$. Suppose also that $T$ is a tree product of $n$ groups ($2 \leqslant n < \infty$) with non-trivial torsion-free locally cyclic edge subgroups, $\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$ is the class of all torsion-free $\mathcal{N}$-groups, and the symbol $\mathit{Poly}_{k}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$ ($k \geqslant 1$) denotes the class of polynilpotent groups such that $X \in \mathit{Poly}_{k}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$ if and only if $X$ has a subnormal series of length at most $k$ whose factors belong to $\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$. We prove that if all free and all vertex groups are residually $\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$-groups, then $T$ is residually a $(\mathit{Poly}_{n+1}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}})$-group. We prove also that if all vertex groups lie in $\mathcal{N}$, then $T$ has a homomorphism onto a $(\mathit{Poly}_{n-1}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}})$-group acting injectively on all edge subgroups. By assuming that $\mathcal{N}$ is the class of all nilpotent groups, we get a stronger result: if all vertex groups are residually $\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$-groups, then $T$ is residually a $(\mathit{Poly}_{n}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}})$-group. It follows that all cyclically-pinched one-relator groups are residually finitely generated $(\mathit{Poly}_{2}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}})$-groups.
item.dc:creator: E. V. Sokolov

item.title: The Andreadakis conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.36302v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $n\ge2$, let $F_n$ be the free group of rank $n$, and let $\IA(F_n)$ be the group of automorphisms of $F_n$ acting trivially on its abelianization. Two natural filtrations of $\IA(F_n)$ are its lower central series $\gamma_c(\IA(F_n))$ and the Andreadakis filtration $\mathrm{I}_{c+1}\mathrm{A}(F_n)$, consisting of automorphisms acting trivially on $F_n/\gamma_{c+1}(F_n)$, $c \geq 1$. Andreadakis conjectured that these filtrations coincide. We prove that the conjectured equality fails for all $n\ge3$ and $c\ge4$.
item.dc:creator: C. E. Kofinas

item.title: Remarks on some maximal subgroups of $F$ and on the $\vec{F}$-index of knots
item.description: arXiv:1910.05045v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We demonstrate that three maximal subgroups of infinite index in the rectangular subgroup \( K_{(2,2)} \) of the Thompson group \( F \), each containing Jones's \( 3 \)-colorable subgroup \( \mathcal{F} \), can be characterized as stabilizer subgroups. Additionally, we show that the \( \vec{F} \)-index, an elementary knot invariant introduced thanks to Jones's construction of knots from Thompson groups, may increase at most by $4$ after changing the orientation of a knot.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Revista de la Uni\'on Matem\'atica Argentina 69 (2) (2026), pp. 443-458
item.dc:creator: Valeriano Aiello

item.title: The model theory of the curve graph
item.description: arXiv:2008.10490v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we develop a bridge between model theory, geometric topology, and geometric group theory. In particular, we investigate the Ivanov Metaconjecture from the point of view of model theory, and more broadly we seek to answer the general question: why does the curve graph of a surface play such a central role in the study of surfaces and mapping class groups? More specifically, we consider a surface $\Sigma$ of finite type and its curve graph $\mathcal C(\Sigma)$, and we investigate its first-order theory in the language of graph theory. Crucially, $\mathcal C(\Sigma)$ is bi-interpretable with a certain object called the augmented Cayley graph of the mapping class group of the surface. We use this bi-interpretation to prove that the theory of the curve graph is $\omega$--stable, to compute its Morley rank, and to show that it has quantifier elimination with respect to the class of $\forall\exists$--formulae. We also show that many of the complexes which are naturally associated to a surface are interpretable in $\mathcal C(\Sigma)$. This shows that these complexes are all $\omega$--stable and admit certain a priori bounds on their Morley ranks. We are able to use Morley ranks to prove that various complexes are not bi--interpretable with the curve graph. As a consequence of quantifier elimination, we show that algebraic intersection number is not definable in the first order theory of the curve graph. Finally, we prove that the curve graph of a surface enjoys a novel phenomenon that we call interpretation rigidity. That is, if surfaces $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$ admits curve graphs that are mutually interpretable, then $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$ are homeomorphic to each other. Along the way, numerous technical results are obtained.
item.dc:creator: Valentina Disarlo, Thomas Koberda, J. de la Nuez Gonz\'alez

item.title: Rubik's as Galois': the inverse Galois problem for the Rubik's Cube group
item.description: arXiv:2411.11566v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the Rubik's cube group can be realized as a Galois group over the rationals.
item.dc:creator: M. Mereb, L. Vendramin

item.title: Partial character tables for $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$-spetses
item.description: arXiv:2507.08502v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let ${\mathbb{G}}$ be a simply connected ${\mathbb{Z}}_\ell$-spets, let $q$ be a prime power, prime to $\ell$ and let $S$ be the underlying Sylow $\ell$-subgroup. Firstly, motivated by known formulae for values of Deligne-Lusztig characters of finite reductive groups, we propose a formula for the values of the unipotent characters of ${\mathbb{G}}(q)$ on the elements of $S$. Using this, we explicitly list the unipotent character values of the ${\mathbb{Z}}_2$-spets $G_{24}(q)$ related to the Benson-Solomon fusion system Sol$(q)$, and the Aguad\'{e} ${\mathbb{Z}}_5$-spets $G_{29}(q)$. Secondly, when $\ell > 2$ is a very good prime for ${\mathbb{G}}$, the Weyl group $W$ of ${\mathbb{G}}$ has order coprime with $\ell$, and $q\equiv1\pmod\ell$ we introduce a formula for the values of characters in the principal block of ${\mathbb{G}}(q)$ which extends the Curtis-Schewe type formulae for groups of Lie type, and which we show to satisfy a version of block orthogonality. In both cases we formulate and provide evidence for several conjectures concerning the proposed values.
item.dc:creator: Radha Kessar, Gunter Malle, Jason Semeraro

item.title: Catalan Semirings
item.description: arXiv:2510.05045v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study Catalan semirings, which are additively idempotent semirings whose multiplicative semigroups belong to a natural family of transformation monoids known as Catalan monoids. There are two kinds of Catalan semirings, whose properties differ substantially. We address the Finite Basis Problem for individual Catalan semirings of each kind and their representations by Boolean triangular matrices. Furthermore, we characterize the varieties and pseudovarieties generated by all Catalan semirings of each kind.
item.dc:creator: Sergey V. Gusev, Mikhail V. Volkov

item.title: On multiply induced characters
item.description: arXiv:2609.04764v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate finite group structures that yield complex irreducible characters induced simultaneously from two or more distinct subgroups. When such a group is realized as the Galois group of a Galois extension of number fields, this phenomenon implies that multiple subfields share the same Artin $L$-function.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra, 2026, Article 108430
item.dc:creator: Masanari Kida, Kyohei Matsukawa, Hikari Watanabe

item.title: Duality and Baire like properties in topological abelian groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.14074v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This article investigates the duality of abelian topological groups by delving into the interplay between the algebraic and topological properties of a group $G$ and those of its dual group. In particular, extending the notion of a $g$-barrelled group, we introduce and study the classes of $\kappa$-barrelled and $\omega$-barrelled groups. Our first main result establishes that every $\omega$-barrelled group is $\aleph_0$-barrelled (i.e., if every weakly convergent sequence in the dual group is equicontinuous, then every metrizable weakly compact subset of the dual group is also equicontinuous). From this, we deduce that the free topological abelian group $A(K)$ over a metrizable compact space $K$ is determined by the subgroup generated by any of its dense subsets. Furthermore, we prove that if $G$ is a $\sigma$-compact, $\omega$-barrelled group, then its dual group $\widehat{G}_\kappa$ equipped with the compact-open topology is sequentially complete (complete if $G$ is hemicompact). We also solve an open question posed by Trigos-Arrieta by constructing an explicit example of an $\omega$-barrelled metrizable group that fails to be $g$-barrelled. Finally, we investigate the dualization of groups lacking infinite compact subsets, proving that for a totally bounded abelian group $G$, every compact subset of $G$ is finite if and only if its dual group $\widehat{G}$, endowed with the finite-open topology, is unordered Baire-like.
item.dc:creator: Mar\'ia V. Ferrer, Salvador Hern\'andez, Isabel Sep\'ulveda

item.title: QWEP stability under twisted crossed products
item.description: arXiv:2610.03424v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the QWEP property of twisted crossed products and its relation to Fourier multiplier transference on noncommutative $L_p$-spaces. We show that QWEP is not preserved by crossed products of QWEP von Neumann algebras by hyperlinear groups. Our examples include trace-preserving actions of a torsion-free residually finite Kazhdan group on a diffuse abelian algebra and on the hyperfinite type II$_1$ factor. We also obtain non-QWEP crossed products with nontrivial scalar cocycles. For scalar twists, we prove that a finite trace-preserving crossed product is QWEP if and only if its ordinary crossed product and its twisted group von Neumann algebra are QWEP. In the positive direction, we establish a restriction theorem for scalar twists of regular wreath products. These results provide QWEP inputs for Fourier multiplier transference and identify a completely bounded multiplier norm obstruction to QWEP. Finally, operator-valued cocycles give finite QWEP crossed products whose acting groups are not hyperlinear.
item.dc:creator: Kai Zeng

item.title: A Non-linearizable Action of $S_3$ on Free Metabelian Lie and Associative Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.26060v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $M$ be the free metabelian Lie algebra of rank $4$ over the field of complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$. We construct a non-linearizable action of the symmetric group $S_3$, the smallest nonabelian group, on $M$ by automorphisms. We also construct a non-linearizable action of $S_3$ on free metabelian associative algebras of rank $4$.
item.dc:creator: Altyngul Naurazbekova, Ualbai Umirbaev

item.title: The Penrose Correspondence over a Non-Archimedean Field
item.description: arXiv:2610.31379v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let \(K\) be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from \(2\), and let \(V\) have dimension four over \(K\). The Drinfeld upper half-spaces of \(V\) and \(\Lambda^2V\) define compatible open analytic subsets of \(\Pp(V)\), \(\Gr(2,V)\), and \(\Flag(1,2;V)\). Both restricted incidence projections are smooth and surjective. For every torsion-free discrete subgroup of \(\PGL(V)(K)\), the three actions are free and properly discontinuous, and the incidence correspondence descends to smooth analytic quotients. These domains contain an explicit flag defined over an unramified extension of degree seven. A symplectic form on \(V\) equips the projective domain with a contact structure and places the Grassmannian domain in \(\Sp_4/(\Sp_2\times\Sp_2)\). For torsion-free discrete symplectic groups, this contact structure descends to the quotient. Free discrete symplectic groups of every finite rank at least two give contact threefolds whose underlying Berkovich spaces have the homotopy type of a bouquet of circles. Every quotient of the projective domain by a torsion-free discrete group preserving the contact distribution is noncompact. For every torsion-free discrete projective linear group, the flag quotient and all fibers of its two incidence projections are noncompact; both projections are nonproper.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Verjovsky

item.title: Every group is the automorphism group of a set-theoretic solution of the Yang--Baxter equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.39228v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give an affirmative answer to the \emph{abstract group problem} for the category $\YB$ of all set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter (YB) equation: every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a YB-solution, which can be chosen on a finite set if the group is finite. In the terminology of L\'aszl\'o Babai, this means that the category $\YB$ is \emph{universal} and \emph{finitely universal}, which is an analogue of Frucht's classical theorem for graphs. Furthermore, the YB-solutions can be chosen within three very small classes: the solutions of the Frobenius-Separability equation, the solutions of the Baaj--Long--Skandalis equation and the recently introduced bipartite solutions. The proof is based on new constructions which associate to any graph a YB-solution in each of these classes, with the same automorphism group as the graph. Explicit YB-solutions with automorphism groups $C_n$, $S_n$, $D_n$ and $Q_8$ are given, as well as a unitary YB-solution, constructed directly from a field $K$, whose automorphism group is ${\rm Aut} (K)$.
item.dc:creator: G. Militaru

item.title: Cutoff for random Cayley graphs of finite groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.41347v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the random walk on a Cayley graph of a finite group whose generators are chosen independently and uniformly at random. We show that, for every finite group, the walk exhibits cutoff with high probability whenever the number of generators is at least a constant multiple of the logarithm of the order of the group and small compared with every positive power of it. This holds for both undirected and directed Cayley graphs, in discrete and continuous time, and the lower bound on the number of generators is best possible, up to the value of the constant. The cutoff time is the time at which the expected entropy of the walk comes close to its maximum, and in general it depends on the structure of the group. This settles a conjecture of Aldous and Diaconis.
item.dc:creator: Haoran Zhu
